contracts.commit_point: The agent's model-call step, where the registered middleware counts each model invocation against thread_limit/run_limit and ends the run or raises once the limit is reached, before further model invocation.
contracts.declared_mechanism: ModelCallLimitMiddleware(thread_limit, run_limit, exit_behavior) returned by create_model_call_limit_middleware, registered in the agent's middleware list via create_agent_with_memory, which supplies the checkpointer required for thread limiting.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Model calls exceeding the configured thread_limit and/or run_limit, i.e., unbounded model invocation (infinite agent loop) continuing past the registered cap.
pending_binding_information: The concrete transport/provider request behind each model call is not shown in supplied source; the http stratum is assigned at the model-invocation commit point as a classification, and should be confirmed against the library implementation.
contracts.protected_operation: Counting and capping of the agent's model-call invocations per run and per thread, terminating or raising at the limit.
contracts.protected_resource: The agent's configured chat-model invocation path within agent runs and threads.
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent model invocations must not exceed the per-thread and/or per-run limits configured in ModelCallLimitMiddleware (e.g., agent infinite loops), with exit_behavior 'end' stopping the run gracefully or 'error' raising an exception at the limit; the middleware must be registered in the agent's middleware list and thread limiting requires a checkpointer.
scope_limits: Covers model invocations only; tool executions are governed by ToolCallLimitMiddleware (separate contract).
Behavior at the limit is selected by exit_behavior ('end' graceful stop vs. 'error' exception).
Thread-level limiting requires a checkpointer (stated at line 401); the example provisions one via create_agent_with_memory(checkpointer_type='inmemory').
Counting and termination internals are LangChain library code not included in supplied source.

contracts.commit_point: Each agent tool call during a run/thread, where the registered middleware counts the invocation against thread_limit/run_limit and blocks calls beyond the cap before further tool execution.
contracts.declared_mechanism: ToolCallLimitMiddleware(tool_name, thread_limit, run_limit) returned by create_tool_call_limit_middleware, registered in the agent's middleware list; multiple instances can be combined (global limiter plus per-tool limiters).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Tool calls exceeding the configured thread_limit and/or run_limit (globally or for the named tool), i.e., excessive tool usage beyond the registered cap.
pending_binding_information: Concrete over-limit behavior (skip, end run, or raise) is not shown in supplied source; 'Prevents excessive tool usage' is the only stated behavior.
Whether thread_limit persistence for tools requires a checkpointer is not stated; the example registers via create_agent_with_tools without a checkpointer.
contracts.protected_operation: Counting and capping of agent tool executions per thread and per run.
contracts.protected_resource: Tools registered on the agent (example: search_tool, database_tool), optionally scoped to a single named tool (example: tool_name='search').
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent tool invocations must not exceed the per-thread and/or per-run call limits configured in ToolCallLimitMiddleware (global, or scoped to a specific tool_name), enforced where the middleware is registered in the agent's middleware list at the tool-call dispatch point.
scope_limits: Covers tool-call counting/capping only; model-call limits are a separate middleware and separate contract.
Global vs. per-tool scoping depends on the tool_name parameter (None means global limit).
Over-limit enforcement internals are LangChain library code not included in supplied source; only the wrapper configuration and registration are shown.

contracts.commit_point: The circuit check at the start of RetryManager.retry (lines 165-167), which raises CircuitBreakerOpenError before the first attempt of func(*args, **kwargs) at line 176.
contracts.declared_mechanism: RetryManager circuit breaker: CircuitBreakerConfig(failure_threshold, recovery_timeout, success_threshold) supplied as circuit_config; _can_execute() state check at the start of retry() raising CircuitBreakerOpenError when blocked; failure recording transitions CLOSED->OPEN and HALF_OPEN->OPEN; reset via reset_circuit_breaker.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Executing func when the circuit breaker state is OPEN and the recovery timeout has not elapsed, i.e., invocation proceeding instead of raising CircuitBreakerOpenError ('Circuit breaker is open'); CircuitState.OPEN is documented as 'Failing, reject requests'.
pending_binding_information: Which concrete operations in the agent stack (if any) execute through RetryManager.retry or with_circuit_breaker is not shown in supplied source; without that, the guard cannot be bound to any agent tool dispatch or lifecycle step.
Whether CircuitBreakerOpenError is intended to gate any agent tool execution, and with what upstream handling, is not established.
contracts.protected_operation: Invocation of the callable passed to RetryManager.retry, gated by the pre-execution circuit check and state machine (CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN with failure and success thresholds).
contracts.protected_resource: The guarded callable's execution path via RetryManager.retry / with_circuit_breaker.
contracts.protection_obligation: A callable executed through RetryManager.retry with a circuit breaker configured (e.g., via with_circuit_breaker) must not run while the circuit breaker is OPEN; the manager must raise CircuitBreakerOpenError before the first func invocation, and the circuit must reopen on failure-threshold breaches or HALF_OPEN failures.
scope_limits: Generic error-handling infrastructure in ai_toolkit/errors; no supplied source binds RetryManager, with_circuit_breaker, or the retry decorator to an agent tool, agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input, so no agent_entry_binding evidence exists and mediation is not_established.

The circuit breaker is active only when circuit_config is supplied to RetryManager; the module-level retry decorator constructs RetryManager without circuit_config (line 518) and therefore does not activate this guard.
The guarded callable is an arbitrary Callable; its concrete external effect stratum is not fixed by supplied source, so the stratum reflects the in-process invocation commit point only.

contracts.commit_point: The agent's tool-execution dispatch step: the middleware interrupts the mapped tool call before the tool executes, pending the human decision.
contracts.declared_mechanism: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(interrupt_on=...) returned by create_human_in_loop_middleware, registered into the agent via the middleware list (middleware=[human_approval] on create_agent_with_memory), which forwards the middleware list and a MemoryManager-created checkpointer (e.g., checkpointer_type='inmemory') into create_agent.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Execution of a tool call named in the interrupt_on mapping without a recorded human decision of approve/edit/reject (i.e., a mapped tool running without the interrupt/approval having occurred).
pending_binding_information: The concrete external effect of send_email_tool (e.g., actual email delivery) is not shown in supplied source; only the tool name and its registration appear.
Exact runtime handling of approve/edit/reject decisions and the post-interrupt resume path live inside LangChain's HumanInTheLoopMiddleware and are not in supplied source.
Whether checkpointer_required=True triggers any enforcement at creation time is unshown; the function body contains only a placeholder comment and 'pass' (lines 357-359).
contracts.protected_operation: Pre-execution interruption of agent tool calls named in the interrupt_on mapping, pending a human approve/edit/reject decision.
contracts.protected_resource: Agent tools registered in the agent's tools list whose names appear in interrupt_on (example: send_email_tool; read_email_tool is explicitly exempted via interrupt_on value False).
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent tool calls whose names are listed in the interrupt_on mapping of HumanInTheLoopMiddleware (created by create_human_in_loop_middleware, e.g., 'send_email_tool' with allowed_decisions ['approve','edit','reject']) must not execute until a human issues an allowed decision (approve/edit/reject); the middleware must be registered in the agent's middleware list and the agent must be created with a checkpointer for interrupt state.
scope_limits: Gate applies only to tool names present in the interrupt_on mapping; tools mapped to False (read_email_tool in the example) are explicitly not gated.

The binding shown is the docstring example path (create_human_in_loop_middleware -> middleware=[human_approval] -> create_agent_with_memory); no production call site and no tool implementation are present in supplied source.

Interrupt state depends on the checkpointer provisioned at agent creation (MemoryManager via create_agent_with_memory); the wrapper itself only carries a checkpointer_required flag and enforces nothing in its body.
Does not cover the other middleware wrappers in this unit (summarization, call limits, PII, shell tool, retries, emulators, etc.).

contracts.commit_point: The agent lifecycle input-processing step (and the output step when apply_to_output=True), where detected PII content is rejected under strategy='block' before downstream model invocation or response delivery.
contracts.declared_mechanism: PIIMiddleware(pii_type, strategy, apply_to_input, apply_to_output, detector) returned by create_pii_middleware, registered in the agent's middleware list; strategies are redact (remove), mask (***), block (reject), hash (SHA256).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Content containing the configured pii_type passing through the agent's guarded input surface (and/or model output when apply_to_output=True) without the 'block' (reject) handling being applied, i.e., rejected-class PII reaching the model or the user.
pending_binding_information: Concrete 'block' rejection behavior (exception vs. content removal, error surfaced to caller) is implemented in LangChain's PIIMiddleware and is not shown in supplied source.
The underlying hook placement (before the model call vs. after the model response) for apply_to_input/apply_to_output handling is not shown in supplied source.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent input-processing and, when configured, model-output handling for the configured pii_type under the 'block' strategy.
contracts.protected_resource: Agent message content at the input/output boundary (user input by default with apply_to_input=True; model output only when apply_to_output=True).
contracts.protection_obligation: Content containing the configured PII type must be handled by the configured strategy at the agent's input/output boundary; under strategy='block', PII-bearing content (e.g., 'api_key' matching detector r'sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{32}') is rejected rather than passed to the model or returned to the user, via PIIMiddleware registered in the agent's middleware list.
scope_limits: Covers the wrapper configuration surface (pii_type, strategy, apply_to_input/output, detector); detection and rejection internals are LangChain library code not included in supplied source.
apply_to_output defaults to False; output-side coverage exists only when explicitly configured.
This contract records the 'block' (reject) strategy as cited by the reviewer; redact/mask/hash transform content rather than reject it and are not covered by this forbidden condition.
